t: Convert Doubly Linked List to Array I
o: Walk the list from head following next pointers, collecting values. All examples are simple traversals; up to 50 nodes.
k: Follow next until null, appending each node's value.

a.i: A single pass over the linked list, appending values to a dynamic array.
s: Initialize empty result and cursor at head.
While cursor exists: append value, advance via next.

w: Trivial; the doubly-linked aspect (prev pointers) is unused here but appears in the harder variant requiring conversion from an array back to a list. No pitfalls beyond null-head handling.
